senses.definition: The path an object follows as it travels around another object in space.
senses.example: Earth takes about one year to go around its orbit.

senses.definition: To travel around another object in space.
senses.example: The Moon orbits Earth.

senses.definition: The attraction between things that have mass. It pulls objects toward Earth and holds planets in their paths around the Sun.
senses.example: Gravity pulls a dropped pencil toward the floor.

senses.definition: A large, nearly round object in space that travels around a star or the remains of a star. Planets in our solar system have cleared most other objects from their paths.
senses.example: Mars is a planet with a rocky surface.

senses.definition: The layer of gases held around a planet, moon, or star by gravity.
senses.example: Clouds form in Earth’s atmosphere.

senses.definition: The feeling that a place or event gives the people there.
senses.example: Soft music gave the room a calm atmosphere.

senses.definition: The Sun and the objects held near it by gravity, including planets, moons, comets, and asteroids. Systems around other stars are often called planetary systems.
senses.example: Earth is one of eight planets in our solar system.

senses.definition: A huge ball of hot gas in space that gives off its own light. The Sun is the nearest one to Earth.
senses.example: A star can look like a tiny point because it is so far away.

senses.definition: A shape with points sticking out from the center.
senses.example: We drew a five-pointed star on the card.

senses.definition: A person who is especially well known for performing or doing something.
senses.example: She became a basketball star.

senses.definition: To play one of the main parts in a show, film, or play.
senses.example: I hope to star in the school play someday.

senses.definition: A natural object that travels around a planet, dwarf planet, or other small world. We call Earth’s own moon the Moon.
senses.example: Ganymede is a moon of Jupiter.

senses.definition: An event in space when one object blocks another from view or moves into its shadow.
senses.example: During a lunar eclipse, Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon.

senses.definition: To block something from view or make it seem less noticeable by comparison.
senses.example: The Moon can briefly eclipse the Sun.

senses.definition: A small, mostly rocky object that circles the Sun. Many of them travel between Mars and Jupiter.
senses.example: A spacecraft can take close-up pictures of an asteroid.

senses.definition: An icy object that travels around the Sun and can grow glowing tails of gas and dust as it warms up.
senses.example: The comet grew a bright tail as it drew near the Sun.

senses.definition: An enormous group of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity.
senses.example: Our Sun belongs to the Milky Way galaxy.

senses.definition: An imaginary or real line around which something turns.
senses.example: A spinning top turns around its axis.

senses.definition: A line on a graph along which values are marked and measured.
senses.example: The bottom axis shows the days of the week.

senses.definition: The turning of something around a center or an axis. The word can also mean one whole turn.
senses.example: Earth’s rotation gives us day and night.

senses.definition: An order in which people or things take turns so each has a chance.
senses.example: The coach wrote down the rotation for each position.

senses.definition: One half of a ball-shaped object, especially one half of Earth.
senses.example: Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere.

senses.definition: A group of living things of the same kind. Members of many species can have young with one another, though scientists also use other clues to tell species apart.
senses.example: The blue whale and the humpback whale are different species.

senses.definition: A part, shape, or trace of a living thing from long ago that was preserved naturally.
senses.example: The footprint in the rock is a kind of fossil.

senses.definition: Change in the traits that living things pass to their young over many generations.
senses.example: Fossils help scientists study the evolution of whales over millions of years.

senses.definition: A feature passed down in a group of living things that helps them survive or have young in a particular place.
senses.example: A snowshoe hare’s broad feet are an adaptation for moving over snow.

senses.definition: A version of a work changed for a different audience or a different way of telling the story.
senses.example: We watched a movie adaptation of our favorite book.

senses.definition: The moving of pollen to a part of a plant that can receive it, a step that can help the plant make seeds.
senses.example: Bees help with pollination when they carry pollen from flower to flower.

senses.definition: The tiny grains that seed plants make and move by wind, animals, or other means. The grains carry cells that help the plant make seeds.
senses.example: Yellow pollen stuck to the bumblebee’s legs.

senses.definition: A way that plants and some other living things use light energy to make sugars. Most plants use water and carbon dioxide to do this.
senses.example: Leaves use sunlight for photosynthesis.

senses.definition: A green substance in plants and some other living things that absorbs light used to make sugars.
senses.example: Chlorophyll gives most leaves their green color.

senses.definition: A plant part that holds a tiny young plant and can grow into a new plant in the right conditions.
senses.example: We planted a bean seed in a cup of soil.

senses.definition: To put seeds in or on the ground so plants can grow.
senses.example: We will seed the bare patch of lawn in spring.

senses.definition: The living things in a place, the nonliving things around them, and the ways they affect one another.
senses.example: In a pond ecosystem, light, water, plants, frogs, and insects all connect.

senses.definition: A small ocean animal with a soft, tube-shaped body. Many corals live in groups and make hard structures that can build up into reefs.
senses.example: Fish sheltered among the branches of a coral.

senses.definition: A pinkish orange color.
senses.example: I mixed pink and orange paint to make coral.

senses.definition: A flow of water or air in a particular direction.
senses.example: The river current carried the leaf past the bridge.

senses.definition: The rate at which electric charge moves through a path, such as a wire.
senses.example: When the switch closes, electric current can flow through the bulb.

senses.definition: Happening, used, or true now.
senses.example: The current plan is to meet after lunch.

senses.definition: A regular rise and fall of the ocean’s water level caused mostly by the pull of the Moon’s gravity. The Sun’s gravity also affects it.
senses.example: When the tide went out, we could see crabs in the rock pools.

senses.definition: A repeating movement, or a single traveling bump, that carries energy from one place to another.
senses.example: A gust of wind sent waves across the pond.

senses.definition: To move your hand or something you hold back and forth, often to say hello or signal.
senses.example: Please wave so I can spot you in the crowd.

senses.definition: A movement of the hand used as a greeting or signal.
senses.example: Grandpa gave us a wave from the porch.

senses.definition: How much matter is packed into a given amount of space. A small block of metal is usually denser than a wooden block of the same size.
senses.example: The oil rose above the water because it had a lower density.

senses.definition: The change from liquid to gas that happens at a liquid’s surface.
senses.example: Evaporation helped the puddle disappear after the rain.

senses.definition: The change from a gas to a liquid. It can happen when water vapor touches something cooler.
senses.example: Condensation made tiny drops on the outside of my cold glass.

senses.definition: Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
senses.example: Our weather chart shows how much precipitation fell overnight.

senses.definition: The ongoing movement of Earth’s water among air, land, the ground below us, and rivers, lakes, and oceans.
senses.example: When water from a lake becomes part of a cloud, it is moving through the water cycle.

senses.definition: Hot, partly or fully melted rock beneath Earth’s surface.
senses.example: Magma collected below the volcano.

senses.definition: Melted rock that reaches Earth’s surface, or the rock it makes after cooling.
senses.example: Lava flowed out of the opening and cooled into dark rock.

senses.definition: A solid material that forms in nature and has its own chemical makeup and a regular pattern inside.
senses.example: Quartz is one mineral found in granite.

senses.definition: A substance such as calcium or iron that living things need in small amounts.
senses.example: Calcium is a mineral your body uses to build strong bones.

senses.definition: A natural solid material made of one or more minerals or other solid substances.
senses.example: We saw three different colors in the rock.

senses.definition: To move gently back and forth or from side to side.
senses.example: The small boat began to rock when a wave went past.

senses.definition: A kind of popular music often played with a strong beat, guitars, and drums.
senses.example: The drummer plays in a rock band.

senses.definition: A large piece of Earth’s stiff outer layer. It moves very slowly compared with the other pieces.
senses.example: An earthquake can happen where two tectonic plates meet.

senses.definition: The wearing away and carrying off of soil or pieces of rock by moving water, wind, or ice, or by gravity.
senses.example: Erosion slowly carried sand away from the bank.

senses.definition: A shaking of the ground that usually happens when rocks suddenly slip past one another deep below the surface.
senses.example: The earthquake made the windows rattle.

senses.definition: An opening in Earth’s surface through which hot rock, ash, and gas can escape. The word can also mean the mountain that builds up around the opening.
senses.example: The volcano’s last eruption left a new layer of rock.

senses.definition: A tiny piece of matter that is still one particular chemical element. Gold is made of gold atoms, for example.
senses.example: An atom of oxygen is so small you cannot see it with your eyes.

senses.definition: A group of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds.
senses.example: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

senses.definition: A basic chemical substance made of just one kind of atom, such as gold or oxygen.
senses.example: Iron is an element used to make steel.

senses.definition: One part or feature of something that has several parts.
senses.example: A surprise ending is one element of this story.

senses.definition: A kind of matter that keeps its own shape under ordinary conditions.
senses.example: Ice is a solid, but it can melt into liquid water.

senses.definition: Made of material all the way through, with no empty middle.
senses.example: The toy was carved from one solid piece of wood.

senses.definition: Firm or strong enough to stay steady.
senses.example: The table needed a solid base so it would not wobble.

senses.definition: A kind of matter that flows and takes the shape of the part of a container it fills.
senses.example: The same liquid fit into a tall glass and a wide bowl.

senses.definition: Able to flow like water or another fluid.
senses.example: Sunshine changed the ice into liquid water.

senses.definition: A kind of matter that spreads out to fill the space around it. Air is a mixture of several gases.
senses.example: Helium is a gas sometimes used to fill balloons.

senses.definition: In American English, a short name for gasoline, a liquid fuel.
senses.example: We stopped for gas before the long drive.

senses.definition: Something that can be passed or stored and that makes changes possible, such as moving things, heating them, or making light.
senses.example: Sunlight brings energy to Earth.

senses.definition: The strength or liveliness you have for doing things.
senses.example: After a snack and a rest, I had more energy for the walk.

senses.definition: A kind of energy that lets our eyes see things when it reaches them.
senses.example: Light from the window fell across the book.

senses.definition: Easy to lift because it weighs little.
senses.example: The empty backpack was light.

senses.definition: Pale in color.
senses.example: I mixed white paint into the dark blue to make it light blue.

senses.definition: To make a place bright or make a lamp start shining.
senses.example: Two lanterns light the path.

senses.definition: A quick back-and-forth or up-and-down movement that repeats.
senses.example: I felt the vibration of the drum when I touched its edge.

senses.definition: A path that electric charge can move through when the path makes a complete loop.
senses.example: Closing the switch completed the circuit and made the toy spin.

senses.definition: A route that brings you back to where you started.
senses.example: We made one circuit of the park before lunch.

senses.definition: An object that can attract certain metals, such as iron, and pull or push other magnets without touching them.
senses.example: The magnet held our drawing against the refrigerator door.

senses.definition: A material that lets electricity or heat move through it easily.
senses.example: Copper is a good conductor of electricity.

senses.definition: A person who leads a group of musicians as they play or sing.
senses.example: We watched the conductor for the signal to start playing.

senses.definition: A person who helps run a train and may check passengers’ tickets.
senses.example: The conductor announced the next stop.

senses.definition: A huge mass of ice that forms on land as layers of snow pile up and squeeze together. It moves slowly under its own weight.
senses.example: In the mountains, a glacier crept down the valley over many years.

senses.definition: The usual pattern of weather in a place over many years.
senses.example: A place with a dry climate may have a rainy day even though most days are dry.

senses.definition: What the air and sky are like in a place at a particular time, including heat, rain, clouds, and wind.
senses.example: The weather was warm before a storm arrived.

senses.definition: To be worn or changed by outdoor conditions, or to get through a hard time.
senses.example: Sun and rain will weather the wooden fence.

senses.definition: A flying mammal with wings made of thin skin stretched over long finger bones.
senses.example: A bat flew over the pond hunting insects.

senses.definition: A club used to hit a ball in a game such as baseball or cricket.
senses.example: I picked up the bat when it was my turn to hit.

senses.definition: To hit, or try to hit, a ball with a bat.
senses.example: Each player will bat once in this practice.

senses.definition: Finding where things are by making sounds and listening for the echoes that bounce back.
senses.example: Some bats use echolocation to find insects in the dark.

senses.definition: To ask someone to pay a price for something.
senses.example: The store will charge two dollars for the notebook.

senses.definition: To put energy into a battery so it can be used again.
senses.example: I plugged in the tablet to charge it.

senses.definition: A property of matter that can be positive or negative. Charges of the same kind push apart, and opposite kinds pull together.
senses.example: A rubbed balloon can pick up an electric charge and stick to a wall.

senses.definition: To rush forward quickly.
senses.example: The players charged toward the ball.

senses.definition: Responsibility for looking after or managing something.
senses.example: I was in charge of feeding the class fish.

senses.definition: A tiny unit that can carry out the basic jobs of life. Living things are made of one or more cells.
senses.example: Under a microscope, we saw many cells in a thin piece of onion skin.

senses.definition: One part of a battery that turns stored chemical energy into electrical energy.
senses.example: Some flashlights use a single battery cell.

senses.definition: One box in a grid or a computer spreadsheet.
senses.example: Type the total in the cell at the bottom of the column.

senses.definition: A small room in a prison or another place where a person lives alone.
senses.example: The old prison cell is now part of a museum tour.

senses.definition: A partly sheltered area near the coast where fresh water from land often mixes with salt water from the sea.
senses.example: Small fish found shelter in the shallow estuary.

senses.definition: An area of land where streams and runoff all drain toward the same river, lake, or other place.
senses.example: Rain that falls in the watershed runs downhill toward the same creek.

senses.definition: A measure in degrees of how far north or south a place is from the equator.
senses.example: A place at 30 degrees north latitude is north of the equator.

senses.definition: Freedom to make some choices about how to do something.
senses.example: Our teacher gave us latitude to choose how we would share our research.

senses.definition: A measure in degrees of how far east or west a place is from a line called the prime meridian.
senses.example: Latitude and longitude together help us find a point on a globe.

senses.definition: An imaginary line all the way around Earth halfway between the North Pole and South Pole.
senses.example: The equator passes through parts of South America, Africa, and Asia.

senses.definition: A way to show the curved surface of Earth on a flat map. Each way changes some distances, shapes, or sizes.
senses.example: The map’s projection made Greenland look bigger compared with Africa than it really is.

senses.definition: An image that light sends onto a screen, wall, or other surface.
senses.example: We watched the projection of the photos on the classroom wall.

senses.definition: A tool that shows how heavy something is.
senses.example: I put the apples on the kitchen scale.

senses.definition: The way a distance in a map or a size in a model compares to the real distance or size.
senses.example: The map’s scale shows that one inch on the page stands for ten miles.

senses.definition: One of the small, thin pieces on the outside of many fish and reptiles.
senses.example: Each scale on the fish caught a bit of light.

senses.definition: A set of musical notes played in order from low to high or high to low.
senses.example: I practiced a scale on the piano before playing my song.

senses.definition: To climb up or over something tall or difficult.
senses.example: The climbers wore safety gear to scale the wall.

senses.definition: A line that shows where one area ends and another begins.
senses.example: The old stone wall marks the boundary between the two yards.

senses.definition: A limit that makes clear what is allowed or welcome.
senses.example: Asking people to knock before entering my room is a boundary.

senses.definition: The city or town where a country’s or state’s main government is based.
senses.example: Boston is the capital of Massachusetts.

senses.definition: An uppercase form of a letter, such as A instead of a.
senses.example: Our teacher reminded us to start a name with a capital.

senses.definition: Money or property available to start or run a business.
senses.example: The farmers used some of their capital to buy a new tractor.

senses.definition: One of the largest land areas into which people divide Earth. Different maps sometimes group them in different ways.
senses.example: A map can show the continent of Africa and the countries within it.

senses.definition: A piece of land with water on most sides and a connection to a larger piece of land.
senses.example: We drove down the peninsula with the ocean to our right and a bay to our left.

senses.definition: A group or chain of islands. It can also mean the area of water that holds them.
senses.example: We took a boat between two islands in the archipelago.

senses.definition: A broad area of grassland, often with very few trees. The name is used especially for grasslands in central North America.
senses.example: In summer, wildflowers dotted the tall grass of the prairie.

senses.definition: An open area of grass with scattered trees, often in a warm place with a wet season and a dry season.
senses.example: Zebras grazed on the savanna while birds rested in a tree.

senses.definition: An area of land built from sand, mud, or other material dropped by a river near its mouth.
senses.example: The river split into several channels as it flowed across its delta.

senses.definition: The fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, written as Δ or δ.
senses.example: The uppercase delta looks like a triangle.

senses.definition: Bringing water to land or plants with pipes, channels, or other equipment, especially when rain alone is not enough.
senses.example: The farm uses drip irrigation to send water to the roots of the plants.

senses.definition: A large society with a shared way of life and organized systems, often including cities, trade, or government.
senses.example: People in the ancient Maya civilization built cities and developed ways to keep track of time.

senses.definition: The title for the men and women who ruled ancient Egypt. A ruler with this title is also called a pharaoh.
senses.example: The pharaoh Hatshepsut ordered the building of a large temple.

senses.definition: One sign in a writing system that uses picture-like shapes to stand for sounds, words, or ideas. Ancient Egyptians used such signs.
senses.example: This hieroglyph looks like a bird, but it can be used to write a sound.

senses.definition: A scientist who studies the people of the past through things they left behind, such as tools, buildings, or pieces of pottery.
senses.example: The archaeologist drew a map of where each piece of pottery was found.

senses.definition: Words or signs written, stamped, or cut onto a surface, such as stone, metal, or paper.
senses.example: The inscription on the statue’s base told us who it showed.

senses.definition: A channel or pipe built to carry water from one place to another, sometimes across a bridge.
senses.example: The ancient aqueduct carried water to people living in the city.

senses.definition: A picture or pattern made by fitting together many small pieces of stone, tile, glass, or another material.
senses.example: We used paper squares to make a mosaic of a fish.

senses.definition: A country where leaders govern on behalf of the public and the head of the country is not a ruler who gets the job by birth.
senses.example: In a republic with elections, people can vote for a president or for other leaders.

senses.definition: The basic rules that describe how a government is organized and what it can do. A constitution can also protect people’s rights.
senses.example: The United States Constitution sets out the jobs of the three branches of the national government.

senses.definition: A change or addition made to a formal document, a law, or a proposal.
senses.example: The class voted for an amendment to its rules about cleanup.

senses.definition: An official refusal to approve a plan or proposed law, or the power to refuse that approval.
senses.example: A president’s veto can stop a bill from becoming law unless enough lawmakers vote to pass it anyway.

senses.definition: To use your authority to refuse to approve something.
senses.example: A president may veto a bill after lawmakers pass it.

senses.definition: The group of people responsible for making laws for a country, state, or other area.
senses.example: The state legislature voted on a proposed law.

senses.definition: A way of organizing a country so that power is divided between a national government and governments for smaller parts, such as states.
senses.example: Under federalism in the United States, the national government and the states have different jobs and share some responsibilities.

senses.definition: A person chosen to speak or act for other people.
senses.example: We chose a class representative to bring our ideas to the school council.

senses.definition: Typical of a larger group or good at showing what that larger group is like.
senses.example: One unusually hot day is not representative of the whole year.

senses.definition: The right to vote in an election.
senses.example: Supporters of women’s suffrage worked for women to be able to vote.

senses.definition: An official count of the people who live in a place. The count may also collect other information about them.
senses.example: The United States carries out a census of its population every ten years.

senses.definition: A formal agreement between countries or other governments.
senses.example: The two countries signed a treaty to settle their disagreement about fishing rights.

senses.definition: The set of letters used to write one or more languages. The letters usually have an agreed order.
senses.example: We sang the letters of the English alphabet in order from A to Z.

senses.definition: One beat or part of a spoken word, usually built around a vowel sound.
senses.example: Clap once for each syllable in butterfly: but-ter-fly.

senses.definition: A way a group of people uses a language. It can have its own sounds, words, and ways of putting words together.
senses.example: The two friends spoke different dialects of English and understood each other.

senses.definition: A way to read and write using patterns of raised dots that can be felt with the fingers.
senses.example: A sign with braille let the visitor check the room number by touch.

senses.definition: A way to write down information with a set of signs or symbols.
senses.example: Musical notation shows which notes to play and how long to play them.

senses.definition: A pattern of sounds, beats, or movements as they happen in time.
senses.example: We clapped the rhythm of the tune without singing it.

senses.definition: A practice session for a performance, ceremony, or other event.
senses.example: At rehearsal, we practiced walking onto the stage quietly.

senses.definition: A group of musicians who play different instruments together, often led by a conductor.
senses.example: In the orchestra, the strings began the tune and the woodwinds answered.

senses.definition: A picture made to show a person, often their face.
senses.example: I painted a portrait of my sister sitting near the window.

senses.definition: Making art by transferring a design from a surface, like a block or plate, to paper, cloth, or another surface.
senses.example: In printmaking class we pressed our inked blocks onto paper to make several copies.

senses.definition: Growing different kinds of crops on the same land in a planned order, often to keep soil healthy and reduce pests.
senses.example: As part of their crop rotation, the farmers planted beans in a field that had grown corn the year before.

senses.definition: An animal that carries pollen so it can reach the part of a plant that receives it.
senses.example: A butterfly can be a pollinator when it visits a flower for food.

senses.definition: A place or collection that stores seeds to preserve different plants for the future.
senses.example: The seed bank stored seeds from many kinds of rice.

senses.definition: The store of seeds already in the soil in a place.
senses.example: After rain, some seeds in the soil’s seed bank began to grow.

senses.definition: To control a ball while moving, such as by bouncing it in basketball or with small kicks in soccer.
senses.example: Maya learned to dribble a basketball with either hand.

senses.definition: To let a liquid run in a thin trickle or a few little drops.
senses.example: The rain began to dribble down the window.

senses.definition: In games such as tennis or soccer, a hit or kick made before the ball touches the ground.
senses.example: Her tennis volley went over the net before the ball had a chance to bounce.

senses.definition: To hit or kick a ball before it touches the ground.
senses.example: I stepped forward to volley the ball back.

senses.definition: A place or organization that collects, cares for, and shows objects or works so people can learn about them.
senses.example: The museum displayed a collection of ancient toys.

senses.definition: A place or service where people can read, borrow, or use shared books and other materials.
senses.example: We borrowed a book about sharks from the library.

senses.definition: A collection of related materials kept together for people to use.
senses.example: Our teacher kept a library of animal sounds for the project.

senses.definition: A collection of records saved so people can consult them in the future, or the place that keeps them.
senses.example: The town archive has photographs of the old train station.

senses.definition: To save material in a collection for future use.
senses.example: We will archive the school’s old yearbooks instead of throwing them away.

senses.definition: The kind of money used in a country or shared by several countries.
senses.example: The yen is the currency used in Japan.

senses.definition: To give something to someone and receive something else in return.
senses.example: I will trade a blue bead for a red one.

senses.definition: The buying, selling, or exchanging of goods and services.
senses.example: Trade brings some fruits from warm places to places where they cannot grow.

senses.definition: Work that uses a particular skill people can learn, such as fixing pipes or making furniture.
senses.example: It takes training and practice to learn the carpenter’s trade.

senses.definition: To trade goods or work directly without using money.
senses.example: The neighbors decided to barter tomatoes for a jar of jam.

senses.definition: An exchange in which people trade goods or work directly instead of paying money.
senses.example: We practiced barter by swapping paper fruit for drawings.

senses.definition: An object that orbits the Sun, is nearly round, and shares its neighborhood with other objects of similar importance. It is not a moon.
senses.example: Pluto and Ceres are both dwarf planets.

senses.definition: To carry or guide someone or something to a place or to another person.
senses.example: Please bring your library book to school tomorrow.

senses.definition: To get something by paying money for it.
senses.example: We saved enough to buy a new soccer ball.

senses.definition: To stop and hold something that is moving through the air or trying to get away.
senses.example: I reached up to catch the ball.

senses.definition: To arrive in time to get on a bus, train, or other ride.
senses.example: We hurried to catch the train.

senses.definition: To decide which person, thing, or action you want.
senses.example: We can choose one book to take home.

senses.definition: To act, work on a task, or carry it out.
senses.example: I will do the dishes after the game.

senses.definition: A word used before another action word to make some questions, negatives, or strong statements.
senses.example: Do you like puzzles? I do like them!

senses.definition: To make a picture, shape, or line by marking a surface.
senses.example: Let’s draw a map of the park.

senses.definition: To pull something in a direction or get something from a place.
senses.example: I will draw a name from the hat.

senses.definition: A game or contest that ends without a winner.
senses.example: Neither team scored, so the match ended in a draw.

senses.definition: To take a liquid into your mouth and swallow it.
senses.example: I stopped to drink some water after the race.

senses.definition: A liquid that people can swallow, such as water, milk, or juice.
senses.example: Water is my favorite drink when I am thirsty.

senses.definition: To control the movement of a car, truck, or other vehicle.
senses.example: My aunt will drive us to the museum.

senses.definition: A trip in a vehicle.
senses.example: We took a drive through the hills.

senses.definition: To take food into your mouth and swallow it, usually after chewing.
senses.example: I will eat the peach when I get home.

senses.definition: To move downward or drop, usually because of gravity.
senses.example: Watch the ripe apples fall from the tree.

senses.definition: The season after summer and before winter.
senses.example: Many leaves change color in the fall.

senses.definition: To move through the air, with wings, in an aircraft, or in another way.
senses.example: The young birds learned to fly above the garden.

senses.definition: An insect with a single pair of wings. Houseflies, fruit flies, and mosquitoes belong to this group.
senses.example: A fly landed on the window screen.

senses.definition: To stop remembering something or fail to think of it when you need it.
senses.example: I sometimes forget where I put my hat.

senses.definition: To change from a liquid to a solid because of cold, or make that happen.
senses.example: We froze grape juice in a tray to make little ice cubes.

senses.definition: To stop moving suddenly and stay still.
senses.example: I froze when I heard a deer step onto the path.

senses.definition: To pass something to someone so they can use it, keep it, or have it for a while.
senses.example: Please give me a turn with the telescope.

senses.definition: To bend, break, or move when pushed or pulled.
senses.example: The branch began to give under the weight of the snow.

senses.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.
senses.example: We went home before the rain started.

senses.definition: To fit, match, or belong somewhere.
senses.example: The blue block goes into the square hole.

senses.definition: To get bigger or develop over time, or to make a plant develop by taking care of it.
senses.example: The bean plants grew taller each week.

senses.definition: To gradually become different.
senses.example: The room grew quiet as the play began.

senses.definition: To put yourself or something else where it cannot easily be seen or found.
senses.example: She hid behind the tree during the game.

senses.definition: The skin of a large animal, sometimes prepared for use as leather.
senses.example: The old drum had a cover made from an animal hide.

senses.definition: To have something in your hand, arms, or another secure place.
senses.example: I held the cup with both hands.

senses.definition: To have room for a particular amount of something.
senses.example: The pitcher holds enough water for four glasses.

senses.definition: To have learned or understood something so that you can remember or use it.
senses.example: I know how to count by sixes.

senses.definition: To be familiar with a person, place, or thing from experience.
senses.example: Do you know the people who live next door?

senses.definition: To guide people or animals by showing them where to go or what to do.
senses.example: We took turns leading the group down the trail.

senses.definition: A position ahead of the other people or teams in a contest.
senses.example: The blue team kept its lead until the final minute.

senses.definition: A heavy, soft metal that was once used for many things, including weights and old pipes.
senses.example: The museum label said the old weight was made of lead.

senses.definition: To go away from a place or person.
senses.example: We left the park before the gates closed.

senses.definition: To let something stay in one place or condition when you go away or stop working on it.
senses.example: Please leave the note on the table.

senses.definition: To stop having something or be unable to find it.
senses.example: I lost one mitten on the way home.

senses.definition: To finish a game, race, or contest without winning.
senses.example: We might lose the match, but we can still play our best.

senses.definition: To create or put something together.
senses.example: We made a bird feeder from things we had at home.

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to act, feel, or change in a certain way.
senses.example: The joke made me laugh.

senses.definition: To come together with someone, whether you planned it or not. It can also mean being introduced for the first time.
senses.example: I met my new neighbor at the playground.

senses.definition: To touch or join at a place.
senses.example: The two paths meet near the bridge.

senses.definition: To work out the meaning of written words or signs, by sight, touch, or another method.
senses.example: We read the trail sign to see how far the pond was.

senses.definition: To say aloud the words that are written down.
senses.example: My brother wanted me to read the poem aloud.

senses.definition: To travel on or in a vehicle or on the back of an animal.
senses.example: I rode my bike around the block.

senses.definition: A trip on a vehicle, animal, or amusement machine.
senses.example: We went for a ride on the merry-go-round.

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, taking quicker steps than when walking.
senses.example: I ran to the big tree and back.

senses.definition: To operate a machine or continue working.
senses.example: The fan can run all afternoon.

senses.definition: To manage the work of a group, activity, or place.
senses.example: The student council helped run the book fair.

senses.definition: An outing or exercise in which someone moves quickly on foot.
senses.example: We went for a run before breakfast.

senses.definition: To speak words or show a message in writing.
senses.example: Mari said we should wait until the light turned green.

senses.definition: A chance to give your opinion or help make a decision.
senses.example: Each team member had a say in choosing the name.

senses.definition: To notice something with your eyes.
senses.example: We saw three birds sitting on a wire.

senses.definition: To understand what someone means or how something works.
senses.example: I see why both pieces need to be the same length now.

senses.definition: To cause a thing, message, or person to go to another place.
senses.example: We sent a postcard to our cousins.

senses.definition: To give off light or look bright as light bounces off something.
senses.example: The full moon shone above the rooftops.

senses.definition: To make something look bright by cleaning or polishing it.
senses.example: I shined my shoes for the concert.

senses.definition: To let someone see something, or help them see how to do it.
senses.example: I showed my friend how to fold a paper boat.

senses.definition: A performance or program for people to see or hear.
senses.example: The school put on a puppet show.

senses.definition: To make music with your voice by moving among notes.
senses.example: We sang a song on the bus.

senses.definition: To rest your body on your bottom with the upper part of your body usually upright.
senses.example: We sat on a bench to rest our feet.

senses.definition: To be in the natural resting state in which you are less aware of things around you and may dream.
senses.example: I slept until the birds started to sing.

senses.definition: The natural period of rest when a person or animal is asleep.
senses.example: A night of good sleep helped me feel ready for school.

senses.definition: To use your voice to say words. It can also mean being able to use a language.
senses.example: She spoke slowly so the whole class could follow.

senses.definition: To stay upright on your feet.
senses.example: We stood at the fence to watch the parade.

senses.definition: A frame or base that holds an object up.
senses.example: The music stand held the pages at the right height.

senses.definition: A small place where people sell or hand out things.
senses.example: A roadside stand sold baskets of berries.

senses.definition: To move through water by moving your body, legs, fins, or arms.
senses.example: The ducks swam across the pond in a line.

senses.definition: To pick up or get something, or carry it with you to another place.
senses.example: I took my jacket when I left for school.

senses.definition: To need or use a particular amount of time, effort, or space.
senses.example: The walk took twenty minutes.

senses.definition: To help someone learn a fact, an idea, or a skill.
senses.example: My cousin taught me a new card game.

senses.definition: To give someone information or say what happened.
senses.example: I told my friend how we found the lost dog.

senses.definition: To notice or work out something by looking, listening, or thinking.
senses.example: I could tell the apple was ripe by how it smelled.

senses.definition: To use your mind to consider something, form an idea, or solve a problem.
senses.example: We thought about where to look for the missing piece.

senses.definition: To believe or expect something without being completely sure.
senses.example: I think the bus will be here soon.

senses.definition: To send something through the air by swinging your arm and letting it go.
senses.example: I threw the beanbag toward the circle.

senses.definition: To arrange and give a party or other special event.
senses.example: We plan to throw a surprise party for Grandpa.

senses.definition: To know what something means, how it works, or why it happened.
senses.example: I understood the directions after seeing someone try the first step.

senses.definition: To have clothing, jewelry, or something else on your body.
senses.example: I wore a warm hat to watch the game.

senses.definition: To become damaged or worn away little by little from use or rubbing.
senses.example: The stones on the path wore smooth after years of footsteps.

senses.definition: To finish in first place or do better than the other side in a contest. It can also mean getting a prize through effort or luck.
senses.example: The green team won its last two games.

senses.definition: To make letters, words, or symbols so someone can read them later.
senses.example: I wrote her name on the envelope.

senses.definition: To create a story, song, message, or other work by deciding what words or notes go into it.
senses.example: We wrote a play about a lost robot.

senses.definition: A young person who has not yet grown into an adult.
senses.example: Each child chose a different color of paper.

senses.definition: A son or daughter of a person, at any age.
senses.example: My father is one of my grandmother’s three children.

senses.definition: One of the hard parts in the mouth that help you bite and chew food.
senses.example: My loose tooth finally came out.

senses.definition: One of several little points that stick out in a row on something such as a comb or gear.
senses.example: A tooth broke off my comb.

senses.definition: A large waterbird with a long neck and feet that help it paddle.
senses.example: A goose and its young crossed the path near the pond.

senses.definition: A small animal with sharp front teeth for gnawing, rounded ears, and usually a long tail.
senses.example: A mouse darted through the tall grass.

senses.definition: A small device you move with your hand to steer a pointer on a computer screen. Its buttons let you select things.
senses.example: I moved the mouse to put the pointer on the picture.

senses.definition: An animal related to a goat, often raised for its wool, milk, or meat.
senses.example: The farmer counted six sheep in the field.

senses.definition: A hoofed animal with long legs. In many kinds, the males grow pointed, branching antlers each year.
senses.example: Two deer stood quietly at the edge of the woods.

senses.definition: The part of a person’s or animal’s body at the end of a leg that touches the ground when standing or walking.
senses.example: I balanced on one foot.

senses.definition: A unit of length equal to twelve inches.
senses.example: The ruler was one foot long.

senses.definition: The lowest part or base of something tall.
senses.example: We stopped at the foot of the hill before climbing.

senses.definition: A single human being.
senses.example: One person stood near the front of the line to help everyone find a seat.

senses.definition: Vibrations that travel through material such as air, water, or a wall and can often be heard.
senses.example: The sound of the bell reached us from across the playground.

senses.definition: To make a noise or to seem a certain way to someone who hears you.
senses.example: You sound excited about your trip.

senses.definition: In good condition or based on good reasons.
senses.example: The builder checked that the old steps were sound.

senses.definition: Facts, objects, or observations that help you check whether an idea is true.
senses.example: The muddy paw prints were evidence that a dog had crossed the porch.

senses.definition: To look at or notice something carefully, often to learn about it.
senses.example: We observe the shadow each day to see how its length changes.

senses.definition: To follow a rule or take part in a custom.
senses.example: The family observes the holiday by sharing a meal.

senses.definition: To look at two or more things to see how they are alike or different.
senses.example: We compared the two maps to see which streets had changed.

senses.definition: To use clues to make a reasonable guess about a number, amount, or size.
senses.example: We estimated how many cups of water could fit in the bowl.

senses.definition: A reasonable guess about a number, amount, or size.
senses.example: My estimate was close to the number of tiles we actually used.

senses.definition: Wanting to know or find out about something.
senses.example: I was curious about how the clock could tell time.

senses.definition: Unusual in a way that makes you wonder about it.
senses.example: There was a curious mark on the underside of the stone.

senses.definition: Easy to break or damage, so it needs careful handling.
senses.example: The thin glass ornament was fragile.

senses.definition: Strong and able to stand up to weight, use, or bumps.
senses.example: We packed the books in a sturdy box.

senses.definition: Able to be trusted to work well, show up, or give information that is usually right.
senses.example: The accurate weather station gave us a reliable record of the temperature.

senses.definition: To say what you think will happen, often based on patterns or other clues.
senses.example: I predict that the ice cube near the window will melt first.

senses.definition: The part of some plants that helps them make seeds. It often has colorful petals.
senses.example: A bee landed on the purple flower.

senses.definition: To grow and open blooms.
senses.example: The tulips flower each spring.

senses.definition: A fine powder made by grinding grain, beans, or similar foods. People use it in bread and many other foods.
senses.example: We stirred two cups of flour into the bowl.

senses.definition: To dust a surface with this powder, often to stop dough from sticking.
senses.example: Please flour the board before we roll out the dough.

senses.definition: To notice sounds with your ears.
senses.example: Can you hear the rain on the roof?

senses.definition: To learn about something from a person or message.
senses.example: We heard that the next game would be on Saturday.

senses.definition: In or to the place where you are or where you are pointing.
senses.example: Put the puzzle pieces here on this shelf.

senses.definition: Two things, people, or animals that go together or are used together.
senses.example: I found a pair of clean socks.

senses.definition: To put two people or things together, or connect one to another.
senses.example: We will pair the new readers with partners.

senses.definition: A fruit that is usually narrow near the stem and rounder at the other end.
senses.example: The ripe pear was soft and sweet.

senses.definition: The salt water that covers much of Earth, or one particular part of that water.
senses.example: From the hill we could see the sea and the boats far away.

senses.definition: Correct or suitable for what is needed.
senses.example: She found the right answer by counting the groups.

senses.definition: The side that is opposite the left.
senses.example: Turn to the right after the bridge.

senses.definition: Something that people are allowed to do or are entitled to have under a rule or law.
senses.example: We learned about the right to vote.

senses.definition: To set something upright again after it has tipped or fallen over.
senses.example: We helped right the empty flowerpot after it fell.

senses.definition: The part of each day between evening and morning when the Sun is below the horizon.
senses.example: At night we could see stars above the trees.

senses.definition: In earlier times in parts of Europe, a trained warrior who often rode a horse and served a ruler. In some places today, knighthood is a special honor.
senses.example: The museum displayed a knight’s old suit of armor.

senses.definition: The chess piece shaped like a horse’s head. It moves two squares in a straight line and then one square at a right angle.
senses.example: The knight can jump over another piece on the chessboard.

senses.definition: Including all the parts, or still in one piece.
senses.example: The whole class listened to the story.

senses.definition: All of something considered together.
senses.example: The four pieces formed a whole.

senses.definition: An opening through a thing, or a space that goes into a surface.
senses.example: A rabbit disappeared into a hole in the ground.

senses.definition: To find out how heavy something is, or to be a certain weight.
senses.example: We weighed the package on the kitchen scale.

senses.definition: To think carefully about different choices or facts before deciding.
senses.example: We weighed the good and bad points of taking two different trails.

senses.definition: A path or direction you can take to reach a place.
senses.example: We asked a ranger for the way to the waterfall.

senses.definition: A method of doing something.
senses.example: There is more than one way to solve that puzzle.

senses.definition: A word used when showing two or more choices, or when saying that something is uncertain.
senses.example: We did not know whether to take our bikes or walk.

senses.definition: A story about something that happened or could have happened.
senses.example: We listened to a tale about a clever rabbit.

senses.definition: The part that sticks out at the back of many animals’ bodies.
senses.example: The dog wagged its tail when we came home.

senses.definition: A long part that sticks out or trails behind something.
senses.example: Our kite had a tail made of ribbons.

senses.definition: One of two or more words that sound the same but have different meanings, such as sea and see.
senses.example: The word pear is a homophone of pair.

senses.definition: A group of words that means something different as a group from what the separate words might suggest.
senses.example: In the idiom “piece of cake,” the speaker means a task was easy.

senses.definition: A word part added at the beginning of another word or word part that helps change its meaning.
senses.example: The prefix re- in rebuild shows that the building happens again.

senses.definition: A word part added at the end of a word or word part. It can change the meaning or how a word works in a sentence.
senses.example: Adding the suffix -less to care makes careless.

senses.definition: Not, or the opposite of. It can describe someone or something that lacks a quality.
senses.example: In the word unfair, un- means not fair.

senses.definition: To reverse an action or take something away.
senses.example: In untie, un- shows that you undo the knot.

senses.definition: Again, as part of a word for doing something another time.
senses.example: If a robot needs a new coat of paint, you can repaint it.

senses.definition: Before, or earlier than.
senses.example: To preview a movie is to see some or all of it before most people can.

senses.definition: Wrongly or in a way that makes a mistake.
senses.example: If you misspell a word, you have spelled it incorrectly.

senses.definition: Without the thing or quality named by the word it follows.
senses.example: A cloudless sky has no clouds.

senses.definition: Having or showing the quality named by the word it follows.
senses.example: A joyful dance shows a lot of joy.

senses.definition: The amount that fits in something.
senses.example: A spoonful of sugar is the amount a spoon can hold.

senses.definition: A person or thing that does the action named by the word it follows.
senses.example: A painter is a person who paints.

senses.definition: More, when comparing two people, things, or amounts.
senses.example: An older dog has lived longer than a younger one.

senses.definition: The state or quality of being a certain way.
senses.example: Kindness is the quality of being kind.

senses.definition: Something so easy it takes little effort.
senses.example: After we practiced all week, the first round was a piece of cake.

senses.definition: To help people feel more comfortable and start talking when they first meet or feel shy.
senses.example: The teacher asked everyone to share a favorite snack to break the ice.

senses.definition: Very seldom or hardly ever.
senses.example: Once in a blue moon, we have pancakes for dinner.

senses.definition: Feeling a little sick or unwell.
senses.example: I felt under the weather, so I rested on the couch.

senses.definition: Understanding a situation in the same way or agreeing on what to do.
senses.example: We read through the rules together to make sure everyone was on the same page.

senses.definition: To begin studying, especially with care and effort.
senses.example: I need to hit the books before the science quiz.

senses.definition: To watch someone or something and be ready to notice a change or problem.
senses.example: Please keep an eye on the cookies while I set the table.

senses.definition: To keep trying or wait patiently when something is hard or slow.
senses.example: Hang in there. The last piece of the puzzle might be under the box.

senses.definition: A very small amount compared with what is needed or with what is already there.
senses.example: One scoop of water was a drop in the bucket compared with what the whole garden needed.

senses.definition: Still deciding between two choices or opinions.
senses.example: I am on the fence about which book to take on the trip.
